title: a-superseded-intention-is-never-silent
owner: CC builds; Akien owns whether a boat riding a superseded intention is ended or re-parented.
intention: Let an intention be superseded or deprecated as a MACHINE-READABLE state, and make that state impossible to pass silently while boats ride it: the deprecating hand gets a report of what is riding (with its own blindness declared), and any boat still riding is refused at its next forward crossing, naming the supersession.
why: Akien, 2026-08-18, reasoning from the graph trees: 'if an intention got superceeded or otherwise depricated, we'd have to also review it's children or in flight whatevers.' Then the correction that shaped the build — 'the ticket is supposed to say what it's intention is already, so that IS the link back, yes?' It is. `owning_intention` is the edge and reversing it is a scan over a directory, so NO BIDIRECTIONAL LINK IS BUILT: the graph tree needed both directions because it is large and in a database; 162 files in git do not, and a stored back-edge would be a second copy of a fact that already exists, with two writers and a drift mode. THE GAP WAS NEVER THE LINK — it is that nothing traverses it and, more basically, that nothing can be superseded at all. MEASURED 2026-08-18: zero of 56 charters carry any supersession or deprecation state; 21 mention the words somewhere in prose, which is exactly the shape `owner` had before `gated_by` — the fact exists in English and nothing can read it. So there is no event, and with no event the only remaining mechanism is a sweep, which is the drift this system names by hand.

falsifier.proves_red: Mark an intention superseded while a boat rides it, then: (a) that boat's next forward crossing REFUSES, naming the supersession and the successor; (b) the deprecation-time scan names that boat; (c) that scan reports how many in-flight tickets it could NOT attribute. Any of the three missing kills it. WRONG-SHAPE, the specific hollow: the scan reports 'no boats riding, clear to supersede' while in-flight tickets carry no owning_intention — a green earned by not being able to see. Today that would be a clean report over 28 boats with 44 invisible. SECOND WRONG-SHAPE: the supersession recorded by editing the charter's existing prose in place, so a record of truth is rewritten to say it was always this way.
falsifier.horizon: the first live supersession of an intention that has boats riding it

children: 44 in-flight tickets carry no owning_intention (measured 2026-08-18, against 28 that do; 64 closed tickets also lack it and are out of scope — a review of what is RIDING does not care about landed boats). NOT CAST: the backfill needs a per-ticket judgement about which intention actually owns each boat, and several of the 44 may honestly have none, which is a question for the corpus rather than a chore for a script. THIS NODE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DEPEND ON IT — see design_choice below.
how: THREE PIECES, and the second is the one that makes the third honest. (1) STATE: charters gain a machine-readable supersession field — the successor's address and the date — written as an ADDITION, never by rewriting the charter's existing prose to say it was always this way (the discipline ruling-door-supersede-path established for ruling packets, cited rather than extended). (2) THE REVERSE READ WITH ITS BLINDNESS DECLARED: harbor_master gains `boats_riding(intention_address)` — the reverse of `boat_owner_of`, same discipline (files only, no daemon, no registry, no network), returning both the boats it found AND the count of in-flight tickets it could not attribute because they carry no `owning_intention`. A scan that reports only what it found is the exact hollow this node exists to forbid. (3) THE REFUSAL, AT A DOOR THAT IS ALREADY OPEN: harbor_master.clearance already resolves boat -> ticket -> owning_intention -> charter -> gated_by, so it is already holding that charter open. It reads one more field. A boat whose owning intention has been superseded is refused at its next forward crossing, naming the supersession and the successor. NOT AT THE CHARTER-WRITE DOOR, and the reason is load-bearing: recompile_gate.sh never blocks its caller and always exits 0 by charter, because that is what makes it safe to fire on every write — putting a refusal there would destroy the property that makes it usable.

watchme.trigger: every supersession of an intention — the act of writing the supersession field to a charter. Fires on the act; no clock, no sweep, no daemon.
watchme.enough: three live supersessions in which the scan's blind count was reported alongside its findings AND no boat riding a superseded intention reached a forward crossing without being refused. Three because a supersession of an intention with zero boats proves nothing about the interesting case, and the blind count earns trust only once it has been non-zero and acted on. EARLY STOP if the first supersession shows the refusal firing on a boat the scan had missed — that is the blindness being real, and it converts the child above from a chore into the next build.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, carrying the scan's output VERBATIM — findings and blind count together, because a scan reported as only what it found is the shape this node forbids
watchme.nexus: the harbor_master's own tree; the deprecation report is the consumer surface
watchme.consumer: the hand superseding the intention, who is deciding whether to proceed, and Akien, who owns whether a riding boat is ended or re-parented

chart_claim: validate-20260818T192832-e2bd14803222 — chart chain complete with real content; verdict berthed at verdict-20260818T194738-1b5e1bb3a84f
design_choice_the_node_turns_on: THE SCAN DECLARES ITS BLINDNESS INSTEAD OF REQUIRING A CLEAN CORPUS FIRST. The alternative — backfill all 44, then build the review — makes the mechanism wait on a chore, and makes its first green a claim about coverage nobody re-measures afterwards. Declaring the blind count means the mechanism is honest at 28/72 today and improves monotonically as the field fills, with the number visible in every report. It is the same move as labelling a coarse measurement coarse rather than waiting to build the instrument (Law 10's operative distinction).

open_at_cast.what_a_superseded_intention_does_to_a_bo: The gate refuses and names the supersession. Whether the boat is ended, re-parented onto the successor, or allowed through anyway is an owner's decision (Law 6), and this node does not decide it. The refusal is a stop, not a verdict on the work.
open_at_cast.an_intention_with_no_owning_boats_is_ind: The blind count makes this visible rather than solving it. Until the 44 are attributed, 'no boats riding' always means 'none among the 28 I can see'.
open_at_cast.whether_supersession_needs_a_door_of_its: Today the supersession is a charter field a hand writes, gated by that charter's gated_by like any other charter write. If supersession turns out to need its own intake (a packet, a reason, a successor that must resolve), that is a later node — not built now, because build-minimal, and because one live supersession will say more than the speculation would.

the_hand_count_was_superseded_by_the_ins: MEASURED 2026-08-18 by the thing this ticket built (cairn.devices.harbor_master.clearance.riders_of, fired through the read face): 69 in flight, 22 attributable, 40 unattributed, 7 unresolvable, 3 UNREADABLE. The numbers written at cast — '28 boats with 44 invisible', '29 with / 43 without', '21 of 72 truly attributable' — came from a hand sweep that did neither of the two things the instrument does: it did not filter to IN FLIGHT (it counted every ticket file, terminal ones included) and it did not PARSE the workflow string (it matched brackets by eye). Those two omissions are the whole of the delta; the shape of the finding — most of the fleet is invisible to an owning-intention read — held. THE CAST-TIME NUMBERS ARE LEFT WHERE THEY STAND, in the falsifier and in design_choice_the_node_turns_on, byte-identical: they are what the wrong-shape was written against, and rewriting them would make this ticket say it was always right (the ticket's own SECOND WRONG-SHAPE, turned on itself). A THIRD BLIND CLASS WAS NOT PREDICTED: three tickets carry prose where a cursor belongs and their flight status cannot be judged at all (a-judge-declares-its-attendance, the-postman-rides, the-route-sieves-carve-out-of-inference-domain). The cast imagined two classes; the corpus has three, and the third is reported as its own rather than folded into 'not riding'. AND ONE OF THE UNRESOLVABLE WAS MINE: the-method-transfers-across-substrates named 'cairn/press_office/intention+why.json' — a doubled root, written by me earlier the same day — which is why the count reads 7 here and 8 in the PROVEME note taken before the fix. The other seven are REPORTED, not fixed; they are the child this ticket names.
proved_2026-08-18: PROVED 2026-08-18T19:51:11, cleared through the harbor's own gate (13 checks, four gates clean) onto cairn/devices/harbor_master/proofs/test_clearance.py sealed green under netns at 19:51:03. Verdict artifact: /home/akien/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/verdict-20260818T194738-1b5e1bb3a84f.json — 8 of 8 criteria pass, 7 hypotheses confirmed, 3 killed. THE DISTINCTIONS WORTH CARRYING. (1) THE STATE LIVES ON THE SUPERSEDED CHARTER, NOT THE SUCCESSOR — the inverse of ruling.supersede(), and deliberately. A retired ruling packet is SIGNED, so its supersession has to land somewhere the signature does not cover; a charter is an authored record that grows by ADDITION, so the key can sit on the retired thing itself. Two more reasons made it not merely allowable but right: a successor-side read would cost a 56-charter scan at every crossing, where the boat's own owning_intention is one open; and a deprecation with NO successor has to be expressible, which is why superseded_by is nullable and the refusal still fires without it. What DID transfer from the ruling door is the discipline, not the shape: evidence required, normalise on READ never by rewriting standing prose, and name every lack in one pass. (2) A WALL IS NOT A GATE. The refusal binds FORWARD crossings only; a boat riding a retired intention may still RETREAT, because the thing being refused is progress under a dead why, not motion. Retreating is what a boat SHOULD do here, and a refusal that also blocked it would trap the fleet it was meant to warn. (3) THE REVERSE READ IS BLIND OUT LOUD. riders_of returns what it found AND what it could not attribute, as COUNTED fields — a scan reporting only its hits is a green earned by not looking. The prediction was 43 unattributed / 8 unresolvable / 0 unreadable over 72 boats; the instrument measured 40 / 7 / 3 over 69 in flight, and the third class was predicted EMPTY: three tickets carry prose where a bracketed cursor belongs and their flight status cannot be judged at all. Folding those into 'not riding' would have made three unjudgeable boats read as three definitely-not-riding ones. (4) THE PARTITION USED TO BE TRUE BY ARITHMETIC. Riders.attributable started as a DERIVED property, so deleting a blind class raised it by exactly as much and every check stayed green under mutation. The mutation tooth caught it on its first run; it is now a counted field incremented in the walk, and the mutation is re-run externally against the file on disk (three classes deleted in turn, exit 1 each, green control between). ONE WRONG-CONDITION CONTROL IS ON THE RECORD because it read exactly like a clean negative: the third mutation's sed assumed a trailing comma the last dict entry does not have, silently did not apply, and the suite exited 0. (5) THE REGISTER AND THE READ ANSWER DIFFERENT QUESTIONS AND RECONCILE EXACTLY: register calls 162 tickets open ('has this left the folder'), riders_of finds 69 ('is this boat still moving'), and 162 = 69 + 90 done-but-not-berthed (register's own filed edge (c)) + 3 unjudgeable. Criterion 2's own wording was FALSIFIED in the doing — it claimed equality with an in-flight count register does not report — and is recorded as falsified, which the validate berth had pre-registered as unknown #2. (6) A SEAL'S HORIZON CLOSES ON ANY .py IN THE COMPONENT, INCLUDING A DOCSTRING. Sealed twice too early this voyage: once when the probe module landed six minutes later, once when a docstring correction to clearance.py landed one minute later. Both times standing() correctly said the code had moved under the proof. Seal AFTER all of the component's code lands, docstrings included. WHAT IS PROVED AND WHAT IS NOT: the read half is proved LIVE against the real corpus; the refusal half is proved in fixture only, because no intention in the corpus is retired today. That gap is claimed by no criterion on purpose — answering it is the probe's job, and the probe's `enough` fires on the ticket's own early stop (the gate refusing a boat the retiring hand's scan had not listed), never on the blind count, which is already non-zero and would have cleared the watch on the day it was armed. LEFT STANDING, REPORTED NOT FIXED: 40 in-flight tickets with no owning_intention, 7 unresolvable addresses, 3 unreadable states, and 41 of 56 charters with no gated_by. They are the child this ticket names.
chart_feedback_2026-08-18: A HAND'S ACT (nothing counts these yet — ticket the-builds-tool-calls-are-evidence-about-the-chart).
